question.problem: Suppose $B$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $det(B)=102.$ The matrix $C$ is obtained from $B$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{2}:=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2}.$ What is the value of $det(C)?$

current_example.problem: Suppose $A$ is a $6 \times 6$ matrix and $\det(A) = 32.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operation $R_3:= \dfrac{1}{8} R_3$. What is the value of $\det(B)?$
current_example.worked_solution:
The row operation applied to $A$ consists of multiplying a row by the number $\dfrac{1}{8}.$

When we do this, the determinant is multiplied by the same number. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =\frac{1}{8}det(A) \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot 32 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
